title: Local Wasserstein Modulus for Two-Atom Latent Treatment-Effect Laws at Proxy Collisions
gap_reasons: The broader SPO setting invoked as the application receives only a lower-bound embedding; neither the sharp upper modulus nor the attaining confidence image transfers to real-valued or additional proxy coordinates.

The claim that the confidence image is computable is supported only by fixed-dimensional semialgebraic representability, with no implemented algorithm, complexity assessment, or numerical evidence showing that the proposed set is practically obtainable and informative.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a two-sided local modulus and matching honest confidence-image diameter theorem for the fixed binary two-proxy specialization. The D0.5 decision and math reviewers passed the repaired package, but the cold general referee rated it subfield because the upper bound and attaining construction do not extend to the broader SPO setting and practical computation was not established. No F-stage Lean formalization was attempted; a field-level continuation would need a broader upper theory or substantial computational validation.
tldr: The paper proves the sharp center-stratified local Wasserstein modulus \(F_s(\varepsilon;\gamma,\kappa)\) for the positive two-atom latent treatment-effect law in the binary two-proxy specialization. The exact binary reduction is implemented on the full-data space using independent auxiliary uniforms to construct both randomized binary potential outcomes, and the refreshed uniform affine upper lemma controls opposite-signed arm contrasts, prognosis arbitrarily close to zero, and renewed growth beyond \(\varepsilon=s^2\). The signed-remainder OEQ is therefore resolved directly by that existing lemma, without a duplicate theorem. A compact sixteen-cell confidence image is globally honest and attains the modulus at radius \(n^{-1/2}\). The binary lower-witness pairs satisfy the quotient-law anchor conditions at the fixed parameterization with two latent classes, \(X=(1,V)^\top\), \(Z=(1,W)^\top\), \(d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=s\); hence the honest-set converse transfers to this specialization and to any comparator class containing those exact pairs. The sharp upper modulus and adaptive image remain binary-only.
gap: Synthetic Potential Outcomes identifies latent treatment-effect mixtures, and the closest quotient-law paper gives collision-uniform \(W_1\) inference at fixed proxy margins. Neither result determines how local uncertainty changes jointly with proxy rank, treatment-arm composition, and the common prognostic contrast at a homogeneous center.
fill: The project derives the two-sided joint modulus, exposes the exact signed affine-remainder lemma on which its upper half depends, constructs legal calibration and rescaling lower experiments for every branch, and transfers the deterministic modulus into one computable globally honest confidence image with matching centerwise expected diameter.
